note_tweet.text:
$META | Muse Ember

While studying interviews with Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang, one particular AI strategy stood out to me.

Push the frontier of intelligence with the most advanced models, then transfer those capabilities into smaller, more efficient models that can serve users at scale.

The launch of Muse Ember shows this strategy taking shape in a real product.

Muse Wonder Full: Used to develop smaller, specialized models.

Muse Wonder: Handles complex reasoning and planning.

Muse Ember: Executes repetitive AI agent tasks at significantly lower cost.

Ember scores 36 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, nearly matching Spark 1.3's score of 37, while operating at approximately 1/17th the cost per task in the reported benchmark.

Why does this matter?

Because AI agents could eventually perform hundreds of tasks per user every day.

In the AI industry, inference economics may become just as important a competitive advantage as frontier model performance.

For Meta, which aims to bring personal AI to billions of people, the real challenge isn't just developing superintelligence.

It's making that intelligence economically viable at a massive scale.

If you enjoyed this post, please like and follow!
